Students will have access to an extensive network of industry contacts to help with optional work experience placements and projects.

Through this course, students will develop their academic writing, their independent research skills and their practical skills in business and accounting software such as Microsoft Excel, Sage and Oracle. The programme is delivered through a blend of lectures, seminars, workshops, presentations and plenary sessions.

Between them, the staff have accumulated an impressive level of academic and professional experience in public audit, taxation, financial and management accounting, and information systems. Occasionally, distinguished external speakers are invited to make presentations on contemporary accounting, finance and business-related issues.

London Metropolitan University places particular emphasis on employability, and the lecturers, who have a wide network of industry contacts, can help students with optional work experience placements and projects.

On completion of this course, students will receive full exemption from all of the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA)’s fundamental exam papers.

This innovative Business Management degree, designed in conjunction with leading industrialists, provides students with insights and understanding of contemporary business themes including entrepreneurship. The course equips students with vital business skills and provides them with an opportunity to practice them in both traditional and virtual business environments. In addition to the degree, students will gain the highly sought after and widely recognised CMI Level 6 Diploma in Management and Leadership.

The University's Business Management BA is accredited at level 6 by the Chartered Management Institute (CMI), an internationally renowned professional body. While studying on this course, students will gain membership to CMI and will be able to access its facilities, attend events, join a mentoring scheme and access over 220,000 live management job postings.

This course will equip students with the key business skills and knowledge needed to succeed in multinational organisations. Students will be provided with an in-depth understanding of all stages of the business management process, from conceptualisation to strategic evaluation.

Students will study a broad range of fields such as finance management, economics, marketing, strategy and human resources, and get the chance to apply their theoretical knowledge to real-life, up-to-date case studies. Students will also hear from specialist guest lecturers, visit a variety of organisations and participate in online business simulations throughout their course. The University’s business incubator, Accelerator, will prove an invaluable resource for flexing their entrepreneurial muscles. Students will have the option to visit the Accelerator facilities and to participate in sessions and competitions.

Students will also have the opportunity to participate in work-based learning as part of their degree. This will give students real-world experience that will set them apart from other graduates when they enter the job market, as well as giving them the chance to put their newfound knowledge to the test.

On completing the course, students will receive their Business Management BA (Hons) degree and a Level 6 Chartered Management Institute (CMI) diploma.

This four-year Business Management (Foundation Year) BA (Hons) degree has a built-in foundation year (Year 0) that provides students with an alternative route into higher education if they don't have traditional qualifications or can't meet the business management entry requirements.

During the foundation year, students will engage with business challenges in a stimulating environment, while boosting their confidence and acquiring crucial academic skills. This acts as excellent preparation for the subsequent three years of study, which will allow students to specialise in more specific and advanced areas of business.

The innovative Business Management (Foundation Year) BA (Hons) degree has been devised with valuable industry input, giving students an edge when it comes to seeking that all-important job when they graduate.

At London Metropolitan University, students will acquire key business skills and knowledge in the classroom but will be provided with a wide range of opportunities outside of the classroom too. The University is home to Accelerator, which provides advice, support, networks, knowledge and resources that can help students turn a business idea into reality. Based in Shoreditch, Accelerator is a unique resource that has helped many students and graduates establish their own businesses.

Students will share their foundation year with students on other business-related foundation year courses. This allows students to share ideas and insights with their classmates before going on to specialise in their subsequent years of study. Should students decide during their foundation year that they’d like to specialise in a different area of business, there is also some flexibility to allow them to do this.

Following the foundation year, students will study the same course content and get the same choice of modules as those who study the Business Management BA (Hons) course. Here, students will have the opportunity to explore decision-making, leadership, organisation design and management, with a range of optional modules to choose from. Alternatively, students can choose to transfer to the Music Business BA (Hons) course if they'd prefer.

Students will graduate with a full undergraduate degree with the same title and award as those who studied the traditional three-year course, but they will also gain a Level 5 Chartered Management Institute (CMI) diploma. As a member of the CMI, students can access their facilities, attend events and access over 200,000 live management jobs and its mentoring scheme.

This Business Management and Human Resource Management degree course is perfect if students want to study business but they are also a people person who wants to help others reach their full potential.

Students will learn how to deal with issues and challenges facing the world of business while also developing the skills needed to attract and retain the right people, at the right time. If they want to, students will also have the opportunity to explore employment law.

This Business Management and Human Resource Management BA (Hons) degree focuses on understanding businesses, the business environment and how to manage the people within them.

Human resource management (HRM) is a key driving force for successful businesses. Because London Metropolitan University recognises this element is so important to business strategy, they’ve developed a course that doesn’t just teach students about core business principles, but also incorporates the people side of things too.

In the first year, students will develop a solid foundation of business management principles that they’ll build on in their second and third year. Students will also learn how to apply business theory to practical scenarios and learn how to acquire, motivate, develop and retain talent.

As the business landscape has changed in recent years, more people are needed to work flexibly across roles. This course is designed to educate students on change management and how to embrace this, aiming to make students more employable when they graduate.

London Metropolitan University's Business Management and Marketing BA degree is a joint honours programme that will provide students with expertise in both disciplines, offering them a greater range of career opportunities on graduation. The variety of skills will make a student an attractive contender for developing their management and leadership career.

London Metropolitan University's course is accredited by the Chartered Institute of Marketing (CIM) and students will receive exemption from two out of three units that are necessary to obtain the CIM Certificate in Professional Marketing. This is a highly sought-after qualification in the marketing industry, especially if students are considering a career in marketing management. The professional certificate means students will be rewarded with two qualifications by the time they finish their studies. This would give students a ‘competitive edge’ in the job market.

As well as developing the skills and knowledge required for either a career in business management or as a professional marketer, the business management and marketing course will provide students with entrepreneurial skills and understanding that will allow them to start their own business.

If students are passionate about starting their own business, they will not only gain the necessary academic knowledge and skills on the course, but also receive encouragement and support through the Accelerator. The Accelerator is a business incubator that helps students make their business dreams a reality by offering mentoring, advice and workshops. Accelerator has supported many successful budding entrepreneurs and can support students with developing any business idea they might have. Through the Accelerator, students will also get the opportunity to enter the Big Idea Challenge for a chance to win a share of the £30,000 prize to launch their business.

This programme is uniquely comprehensive among business management and marketing courses in the UK. In addition to learning broad marketing skills that apply to the commercial world, the programme also provides students with opportunities to develop new specialist marketing skills to help improve society through the relatively new field of Social Marketing. In this new field, students will learn how to apply the latest marketing techniques to social problems, such as obesity, drunk-driving, discrimination and domestic violence. Lecturers will introduce the concepts and history of social marketing based on their own innovative research. Completing this module will give students an advantage when competing for jobs in the third and public sector.

As part of the course, students will have the opportunity to undertake short and long accredited work placements. This opportunity may be strengthened with undertaking another of London Metropolitan University's innovative modules that equip students with skills for employment, such as the Theory and Practice of Selling module. As all business professionals know, selling is an essential function of business and on this module, students will develop vital negotiation and selling techniques that will ensure them success in their career. Past students on the module have found that it has helped them gain recognition from the Institute of Sales and Marketing Management (ISMM), a professional organisation that represents sales professionals in the UK.

This business management and marketing programme not only aims to improve students' career opportunities, but also seeks to accelerate their cultural and personal growth. Students will find opportunities to study abroad for a semester in places such as Europe, Japan or the USA, where they will be immersed in a new culture and acquire new perspectives. International students visiting from London Metropolitan University's partner institutions will also expand students' world view and help students appreciate business management and marketing on an international scale.

Students will learn skills in interactive media content creation, interactive design, digital media production, social media management, digital media project management and much more.

This programme will teach students how to manage successful projects. This will begin with the assessment and selection of the appropriate tools and software applications for producing a digital media project. They'll also learn how to develop digital media and social media strategies.

Students will then study how to manage production teams and communicate effectively in a professional media environment. By the end of the programme, students should be able to confidently navigate the complexity of the international digital media and creative industries.

539v:
This Education MA degree is designed to provide students with a broad range of knowledge and skills within the field of education. This course will provide students with opportunities to develop and enhance their professional skills and understanding, so that students can progress within or embark on a career within the sector.

This diverse course covers a range of disciplines, drawing from areas such as curriculum theory, psychology of learning and human potential, sociology of gender, social class, race, philosophy and the history of education.

This course aims to introduce students to key academic and professional debates within the field, helping them to develop a professional voice and standpoint. Upon successful completion of this course, London Metropolitan University hopes that students will feel enthused about returning to the field and feel intellectually empowered to initiate change.

A key theme embedded in this master’s degree is social justice. This course is aligned with the Education for Social Justice (ESJ) strategy to ensure equity in the curriculum practice.

The modules have been developed to broaden the knowledge and meaning of the term ‘education’, as well as its purpose from being a ‘product’ to understanding how the curriculum is managed and led. Students will also explore its influence on children’s learning, assessment and life chances. This degree has five core 20 credit modules:

  • Curriculum, Pedagogy and Assessment
  • Curriculum Leadership
  • Critical Theory and Education
  • Research Methods in Education
  • Education Dissertation

Specialist option modules allow students to explore subjects that are of particular interest to them in more detail, such as:

  • Applying Learning Technologies
  • Issues in Language Learning: An Intercultural Approach
  • Reflective Practice
  • Social Justice Education
  • Web-based Learning and Teaching
  • Understanding the Language Classroom

If students have a particular interest in studying women abuse, they are also able to choose from the following option modules:

  • Sexual Violence: Causes, Consequences and Interventions
  • Violence against Women: Issues, Research and Policy

If there’s a specific topic students would like to study in more detail that does not appear here, they can choose an alternative education-focused topic in agreement with a subject supervisor.

This diverse course covers a range of disciplines, drawing from areas such as curriculum theory, psychology of learning and human potential, identity and self in the early years, sociology of gender, social class, race, philosophy and the critical discourses in early childhood studies.

This degree aims to introduce students to key academic and professional debates within the field of education and an opportunity to focus on early childhood and the early years, helping them to develop a professional perspective and standpoint. Upon successful completion of this course, it is hoped that students will feel enthused about continuing in the sector and feel intellectually empowered to initiate change.

A key theme embedded in this master’s degree is social justice. This course is aligned with the Education for Social Justice (ESJ) framework to ensure equity in the curriculum practice.

The modules have been developed to broaden the knowledge and meaning of the term ‘education’, as well as its purpose from being a ‘product’ to understanding how the curriculum is managed and led. Education is a creative and powerful endeavour in which curriculum and pedagogy come together to support children's learning whilst widening their future life chances.

This degree can be completed as a postgraduate diploma by taking four core modules and two optional modules. Students could also choose to study for a Postgraduate Certificate in Education by choosing to study the following three core modules: Critical Theory and Education; Curriculum Leadership; Curriculum, Pedagogy and Assessment.

Applications are welcomed from practising teachers and if they already hold a relevant PGCE qualification, they may be able to apply for credit and study fewer modules to complete this MA.

This Master's degree is designed for teachers and language professionals to learn how to teach the English language. The course is also suitable if students don't have any teaching experience.

London Metropolitan University has a diverse cohort so students will benefit from a varied learning experience. Students will explore new theories and conversation around language, teaching languages and learning in various social and educational environments.

Students will explore language pedagogy, linguistics, sociolinguistics in relation to theory and practice on this English Language Teaching MA. Students will also learn about topics such as the psychology of language and language testing.

Students will develop the skills needed to become an employable language teacher, policy maker, educator or researcher. On this course, students will take part in discussions on language, undertake reading and be supported through research, plus students will have the opportunity to go into schools and understand the English language teaching process.

The teaching team are experienced practitioners who have published work and research in the sector. Research topics have included the processes of second language learning and teaching and English as a second language and English as a foreign language in higher education.

This Master's degree explores the sociocultural, political, economic and cultural aspects of how the English language is learned, taught and used worldwide.

The reflexive and reflective element of this course aims to improve in students' practice by encouraging them to think of themselves as a global language professional.

There are no exams. Students will be assessed through a variety of methods including coursework, essays, presentations, research and a final dissertation.

53dl:
The world of business and work is changing rapidly. With automation, AI, online working, climate change and diversity, students will need to be prepared to face and respond to change.

The MBA has been designed using advice and insight from large organisations and business entrepreneurs. This course aims to prepare students for greater business responsibility, switching industries or job roles, or to start their own business.

Students will gain practical skills and experience through business simulations, where they will be making real business decisions to ensure the imitation businesses make a profit and can operate. The first simulation focuses on understanding business finance and accounting, while the second focuses on global strategy. These will involve analysing finances, the supply chain and operations. Most importantly, students will gain experience of working in a team to make decisions in a competitive environment and then deal with the results. London Metropolitan University is one of the few universities in the UK that incorporates business simulation activities into the course.

Students will refine their complex problem solving skills and develop their critical thinking abilities. The MBA will help develop their management skills, how to work effectively in teams, take on the leadership of a diverse group and influence others.

The business world is a volatile environment. Students will study the impact of accelerating climate change, technology development and global politics on the UK’s business economy, learning how to make fundamental business decisions in uncertain times and with incomplete data.

Insights into the wider role of businesses in addressing societal problems in a sustainable manner will also develop their understanding of ethical management and governance.

Students may have had a break from studies and been in the work environment for some time. To help them prepare for the MBA, London Metropolitan University has developed a one-week bootcamp module to help build students develop their skills and knowledge prior to starting the course, so that they can really maximise their learning potential on the course. This bootcamp will help students establish what their specific goals are and serve as a personal development plan to help keep them on track throughout their studies. It’s completed online the week before students start their first module.

Students will be taught by industry specialists in finance, strategy, creativity, marketing, operations coaching and networking, who have years of practitioner experience.

The aim is for students to graduate with a broad understanding of how businesses operate, how they are managed and how they’re governed. This MBA will prepare students for a more senior role in business, a change in career direction or to go on and start their own business.
